s682.content:
Theodore was born at an inn in the village of Sykeon in Galatia, in Asia Minor. As a boy he spent long hours in prayer in a nearby chapel, and he grew into a severe ascetic who lived for a time in a cave and in an iron cage.

He was ordained, founded monasteries, and against his will became bishop of Anastasiopolis, though he later resigned to return to the monastic life. Crowds came to him for healing and help, and a disciple named George wrote a long, lively Life of him.
s682.intercession: St. Theodore, pray for us. Bring healing to the sick, and peace to all who are troubled. Amen.

s683.content:
Lucian was a priest and teacher in Antioch, known for his careful scholarship on the text of the Greek Bible. His revision of the Greek Old Testament and the New Testament was widely used in the churches of Syria and Asia Minor.

During the persecution under Maximinus he was arrested and taken to Nicomedia, where he died for the faith in 312. Eusebius records that he made a speech in defense of the faith before the judge.
s683.intercession: St. Lucian, pray for us. Bless all who study and translate the Scriptures. Amen.

s684.content:
Dionysius was a member of the Areopagus, the high council of Athens, who believed when he heard St. Paul preach there about the unknown god, as the Acts of the Apostles records (Acts 17:34). An early tradition says he became the first bishop of Athens and died a martyr.

Around the year 500 a Syrian writer published deep works of mystical theology under his name, and these writings, by the author called Pseudo-Dionysius, influenced theologians of both East and West for a thousand years.
s684.intercession: St. Dionysius, pray for us. Open our minds to the God who is beyond all knowing, and our hearts to his word. Amen.

s685.content:
Pantaenus was a Stoic philosopher who became a Christian and led the catechetical school of Alexandria, the first great Christian school of theology. His most famous student was Clement of Alexandria, who called him a “Sicilian bee” that gathered the honey of the apostles and prophets.

Eusebius records that Pantaenus also went as a missionary to the East, as far as “India,” where he was said to have found Christians who already had the Gospel of Matthew in Hebrew letters.
s685.intercession: St. Pantaenus, pray for us. Bless all who teach the faith, and give us wisdom joined to love. Amen.

s686.content:
In February 2015, twenty Coptic Christian laborers from Egypt and a companion from Ghana, who had gone to Libya to work and support their families, were beheaded on a beach near Sirte by Islamic State militants. A video of their deaths showed many of them praying the name of Jesus.

The Coptic Orthodox Church soon proclaimed them saints. In 2023 Pope Francis, with Pope Tawadros II, announced that they would be included in the Roman Martyrology, a sign of the “ecumenism of blood” that unites Christians who die for Christ.
s686.intercession: Holy Coptic Martyrs, pray for us. Strengthen persecuted Christians everywhere, and bring all Christians to unity. Amen.

s687.content:
Telesphorus was bishop of Rome for about ten years, from around 126 to 137, under the emperors Hadrian and Antoninus Pius. St. Irenaeus, writing later in the same century, lists him among the bishops of Rome and says that he bore a glorious martyrdom.

The Liber Pontificalis, written centuries afterward, credits him with the custom of a Mass at night on Christmas, though this is uncertain. The 1962 calendar commemorates him on January 5.
s687.intercession: St. Telesphorus, pray for us. Make us faithful witnesses to Christ to the end. Amen.

s688.content:
Hyginus was bishop of Rome from about 138 to 142, when the Gnostic teachers Valentinus and Cerdo had come to the city. Tradition holds that he set out the ranks and duties of the clergy.

The old calendar honors him as a martyr, though the early sources do not say how he died. He is commemorated on January 11.
s688.intercession: St. Hyginus, pray for us. Keep us in the true faith handed down from the apostles. Amen.

s689.content:
Marcellus became bishop of Rome in 308, after the see had stood empty for a long time in the persecution of Diocletian. He insisted that Christians who had denied the faith under persecution must do penance before being received back, and the strife this caused led the emperor Maxentius to banish him from Rome. He died in exile the next year.

His relics lie under the altar of San Marcello al Corso in Rome. The 1962 calendar keeps his feast on January 16.
s689.intercession: St. Marcellus, pray for us. Teach us true repentance and the mercy of God. Amen.

s690.content:
Prisca was a young Roman Christian who was put to death for her faith; the date of her martyrdom is unknown. Her name appears in the ancient lists of Roman martyrs.

The church of Santa Prisca on the Aventine Hill bears her name; tradition links it both to her and to Prisca, the friend of St. Paul. The 1962 calendar commemorates her on January 18.
s690.intercession: St. Prisca, pray for us. Give us courage to confess Christ in every trial. Amen.

s691.content:
According to their sixth-century legend, Marius and Martha were a Persian couple who came to Rome on pilgrimage with their sons Audifax and Abachum. They cared for imprisoned Christians and buried the bodies of martyrs, and were themselves martyred about 270.

The legend is not historically reliable, but the family was honored as martyrs from early times. The 1962 calendar commemorates them on January 19.
s691.intercession: Holy martyrs Marius, Martha, Audifax, and Abachum, pray for our families. Amen.

s692.content:
Martina was a Roman virgin and martyr, honored as one of the patron saints of Rome. Her story, written long after her death, places her martyrdom in the third century.

In 1634 her relics were found in the ancient church in the Roman Forum that bears her name, and Pope Urban VIII, who wrote hymns in her honor, had it rebuilt as Santi Luca e Martina. The 1962 calendar keeps her feast on January 30.
s692.intercession: St. Martina, pray for us, and for the city of Rome. Amen.

s693.content:
Andrew was born into the noble Corsini family of Florence. Tradition says that his mother’s prayers and reproaches turned him from a wild youth to the Carmelite friars, where he became a renowned preacher.

In 1349 he was made bishop of Fiesole. He lived simply, cared for the poor, and reconciled feuding factions. He was canonized in 1629, and the 1962 calendar keeps his feast on February 4.
s693.intercession: St. Andrew Corsini, pray for us. Turn our hearts from sin and make us peacemakers. Amen.

s694.content:
Faustinus and Jovita are the patron saints of Brescia in northern Italy. Tradition holds that they were brothers, a priest and a deacon of the city, put to death for the faith under the emperor Hadrian, around 120.

Their later acts are largely legendary, but their cult in Brescia is ancient. The 1962 calendar commemorates them on February 15.
s694.intercession: Sts. Faustinus and Jovita, pray for us, and for all who serve at the altar. Amen.

s695.content:
Simeon, son of Clopas, was a kinsman of the Lord. According to the early historian Hegesippus, whose words Eusebius preserved, he became the second bishop of Jerusalem after St. James and led that Church for many years.

Under the emperor Trajan, at a great age, he was crucified for the faith. The 1962 calendar commemorates him on February 18.
s695.intercession: St. Simeon, pray for us. Make us steadfast in the faith to old age. Amen.

s696.content:
Anicetus, a Syrian, was bishop of Rome from about 157 to 168. He opposed the Gnostic and Marcionite teachers then active in Rome.

He welcomed St. Polycarp of Smyrna, who came to Rome to discuss the date of Easter. The two could not agree, yet they parted in peace, and Anicetus let Polycarp celebrate the Eucharist in his place, as St. Irenaeus later recalled. The 1962 calendar commemorates him on April 17.
s696.intercession: St. Anicetus, pray for us. Help us keep charity and unity even where we differ. Amen.

s697.content:
Two popes share this day. Soter, bishop of Rome from about 167 to 174, was known for his generosity: St. Dionysius of Corinth wrote to thank the Roman Church for the help Soter sent to Christians in need and to those condemned to the mines.

Caius was pope from 283 to 296. He is traditionally said to have been a relative of the emperor Diocletian, but the old accounts of his life rest on legend. The 1962 calendar keeps their feast on April 22.
s697.intercession: Sts. Soter and Caius, pray for us. Make us generous to all who suffer. Amen.

s698.content:
Cletus, also called Anacletus, was the third bishop of Rome, after St. Peter and St. Linus, from about 80 to 92. He is named in the Roman Canon of the Mass.

Marcellinus led the Church of Rome from 296 to 304, through the outbreak of the great persecution of Diocletian. The 1962 calendar keeps their feast on April 26.
s698.intercession: Sts. Cletus and Marcellinus, pray for us, and for the Church of Rome. Amen.

s699.content:
Tradition identifies this Alexander with Pope Alexander I, bishop of Rome in the early second century, martyred with the priests Eventius and Theodulus. Historians doubt the identification, but the three were honored together as martyrs, and the ruins of a church over their tombs were found on the Via Nomentana in the nineteenth century.

On the same day the 1962 calendar remembers St. Juvenal, the first bishop of Narni in Umbria, a confessor.
s699.intercession: Holy martyrs Alexander, Eventius, and Theodulus, pray for us. Amen.

s700.content:
Antoninus Pierozzi joined the Dominicans as a young man and became prior of the convent of San Marco in Florence. In 1446 Pope Eugene IV made him archbishop of Florence.

He was known for his care for the poor, his writings on moral theology and on commerce and economics, and the simplicity of his life. He was canonized in 1523, and the 1962 calendar keeps his feast on May 10.
s700.intercession: St. Antoninus, pray for us. Make us honest in our work and generous to the poor. Amen.

s701.content:
Nereus and Achilleus were Roman soldiers who, according to an epitaph written by Pope St. Damasus, laid down their arms when they became Christians and died as martyrs. They were buried in the Catacomb of Domitilla on the Via Ardeatina, where a basilica was later built over their tomb.

The 1962 calendar honors them on May 12 together with St. Flavia Domitilla, a Roman noblewoman of the imperial family exiled for the faith, and St. Pancras.
s701.intercession: Sts. Nereus and Achilleus, pray for us, and for all who serve as soldiers. Amen.

s702.content:
According to his legend, Boniface was the steward of a wealthy Roman woman named Aglaë and lived with her in sin. She sent him to the East to bring back relics of the martyrs, and at Tarsus he himself confessed Christ and was martyred, about 307. Aglaë repented and spent the rest of her life in penance.

The story is largely legendary. The 1962 calendar commemorates him on May 14.
s702.intercession: St. Boniface, pray for us. Turn sinners to repentance and to Christ. Amen.

s704.content:
According to tradition, Venantius was a fifteen-year-old of Camerino in central Italy who was tortured and beheaded for the faith under the emperor Decius, about 250, together with his teacher, the priest Porphyrius, and others.

He is the patron of Camerino, where his basilica stands. The 1962 calendar keeps his feast on May 18.
s704.intercession: St. Venantius, pray for us, and for all young people. Amen.

s705.content:
Felix was bishop of Rome from 269 to 274. He wrote a letter on the divinity and humanity of Christ. In his time the emperor Aurelian, asked to settle a dispute at Antioch, ruled that the church there belonged to the bishop in communion with Rome, so that the heretic Paul of Samosata had to give it up.

The old calendar honors him as a martyr, though he may not have died by violence. He is commemorated on May 30.
s705.intercession: St. Felix, pray for us. Keep us faithful to the truth about Christ. Amen.

s706.content:
Ascanio Caracciolo, a nobleman of the Abruzzo, recovered from a grave illness at twenty-two and gave his life to God. As a priest in Naples he joined a confraternity that cared for prisoners condemned to death.

With John Augustine Adorno he founded the Clerics Regular Minor, taking the name Francis. Its members took turns in perpetual adoration of the Blessed Sacrament. He died in 1608, was canonized in 1807, and the 1962 calendar keeps his feast on June 4.
s706.intercession: St. Francis Caracciolo, pray for us. Kindle in us love for Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament. Amen.

s707.content:
Primus and Felician were brothers, martyred about 297 in the persecution of Diocletian and buried at the fourteenth milestone of the Via Nomentana, near Mentana.

In the seventh century Pope Theodore I moved their relics into Rome, to the church of Santo Stefano Rotondo. The 1962 calendar commemorates them on June 9.
s707.intercession: Sts. Primus and Felician, pray for us, and for all brothers and sisters. Amen.

s708.content:
John, a priest from Sahagún in León, studied at Salamanca and joined the Augustinian friars there in 1463. He was the leading preacher of a city torn by feuds between noble families, and he worked tirelessly to reconcile them. He was devoted to the Mass and spoke out boldly against injustice.

He died in 1479 and was canonized in 1690. The 1962 calendar keeps his feast on June 12.
s708.intercession: St. John of Sahagún, pray for us. Make us peacemakers in our homes and cities. Amen.

s709.content:
A Venetian nobleman, Gregory Barbarigo served as a diplomat before he was ordained. He became bishop of Bergamo in 1657 and a cardinal, and from 1664 bishop of Padua, where he carried out the reforms of the Council of Trent, visited every parish, and built up the seminary with a famous printing press.

He worked for reunion with the Eastern Churches. Pope St. John XXIII canonized him in 1960 and added him to the calendar on June 17.
s709.intercession: St. Gregory Barbarigo, pray for us, and for all bishops and priests. Amen.

s710.content:
Silverius, the son of Pope Hormisdas, was made bishop of Rome in 536. When the Byzantine general Belisarius took Rome, Silverius was falsely accused of plotting with the Goths and, at the urging of the empress Theodora, who wanted a pope of her own choosing, he was deposed and sent into exile.

He died of hunger on the island of Palmarola in 537 and is honored as a martyr. The 1962 calendar commemorates him on June 20.
s710.intercession: St. Silverius, pray for us, and for all who suffer injustice. Amen.

s711.content:
Born at Vercelli in northern Italy, William set out as a young man on pilgrimage to Santiago de Compostela and later lived as a hermit. On Monte Vergine near Avellino he founded a monastery, and the community grew into the Congregation of Monte Vergine; its shrine of Our Lady is still a great place of pilgrimage.

He died in 1142. The 1962 calendar keeps his feast on June 25.
s711.intercession: St. William, pray for us. Lead us on our pilgrimage to God. Amen.

s712.content:
According to their acts, John and Paul were brothers, Roman officials who were martyred in their own house on the Caelian Hill under the emperor Julian the Apostate in the 360s. A basilica was built over the house, and excavations beneath Santi Giovanni e Paolo have uncovered Roman rooms decorated with early Christian paintings.

They are named in the Roman Canon of the Mass. The 1962 calendar keeps their feast on June 26.
s712.intercession: Sts. John and Paul, pray for us. Make our homes places of faith. Amen.

s713.content:
An ancient legend tells of St. Felicity, a Roman widow whose seven sons, Januarius, Felix, Philip, Silvanus, Alexander, Vitalis, and Martial, were martyred before her eyes in the second century, like the mother and her seven sons in the Second Book of Maccabees. The legend’s details are uncertain, but the seven were honored at Rome on this day from very early times, in four different cemeteries.

On the same day the 1962 calendar remembers Sts. Rufina and Secunda, Roman virgins martyred in the third century.
s713.intercession: Holy Seven Brothers, pray for us, and for all mothers and their children. Amen.

s714.content:
Pius was bishop of Rome from about 140 to 155. According to the Muratorian Fragment, an early list of the books of the Bible, he was the brother of Hermas, author of The Shepherd.

He opposed the Gnostic teachers and Marcion, who were active in Rome in his time. The 1962 calendar commemorates him on July 11.
s714.intercession: St. Pius, pray for us. Guard us against every false teaching. Amen.

s715.content:
According to a famous legend, Alexius was the son of a wealthy Roman senator who left home on his wedding night to live as a poor pilgrim in Edessa in Syria. Years later he returned and lived unrecognized as a beggar under the stairs of his father’s house, and his identity was discovered only at his death.

The story spread from Syria across the Christian world and has inspired many to embrace poverty for Christ. The 1962 calendar commemorates him on July 17.
s715.intercession: St. Alexius, pray for us. Teach us to seek God above all honors. Amen.

s716.content:
Apollinaris was the first bishop of Ravenna. Tradition makes him a disciple of St. Peter who sent him to Italy; he governed the Church of Ravenna and died a martyr.

The great sixth-century basilica of Sant’Apollinare in Classe, near Ravenna, was built over his tomb, and its apse mosaic shows him at prayer among his flock. The 1962 calendar keeps his feast on July 23.
s716.intercession: St. Apollinaris, pray for us, and for all shepherds of the Church. Amen.

s717.content:
Christina is venerated as a young virgin and martyr of the third century. Her cult is ancient at Bolsena in central Italy, where catacombs and a church stand over her tomb, and the Eastern Churches honor her as Christina of Tyre.

Her later legends are full of marvels and are not historical. The 1962 calendar commemorates her on July 24.
s717.intercession: St. Christina, pray for us. Keep us pure and strong in faith. Amen.

s718.content:
Pantaleon was a physician of Nicomedia in Asia Minor who served the sick and was martyred in the persecution of Diocletian, about 305.

In the West he is one of the Fourteen Holy Helpers, and in the East one of the Holy Unmercenaries, physicians who healed without payment. The 1962 calendar commemorates him on July 27.
s718.intercession: St. Pantaleon, pray for us, and for all who care for the sick. Amen.

s719.content:
Abdon and Sennen were Persian Christians who, according to their acts, were martyred at Rome in the persecution of Decius, about 250.

They were buried in the Catacomb of Pontian on the Via Portuensis, where an early painting shows them in Persian dress. The 1962 calendar commemorates them on July 30.
s719.intercession: Sts. Abdon and Sennen, pray for us, and for all who suffer far from home. Amen.

s720.content:
Two Roman martyrs share this day. Tiburtius, according to the legend of St. Sebastian, was the son of a Roman prefect converted by Sebastian, and he was buried on the Via Labicana.

Susanna’s story, written in the fifth century, has little historical value, but a real martyr named Susanna probably lies behind it, and the church of Santa Susanna in Rome bears her name. The 1962 calendar commemorates them on August 11.
s720.intercession: Sts. Tiburtius and Susanna, pray for us. Amen.

s721.content:
Agapitus was a young martyr of Palestrina, the ancient Praeneste near Rome, put to death perhaps in 274; the Roman Martyrology calls the date uncertain.

Palestrina honors him as its patron, and his tomb there was a place of pilgrimage from early times. The 1962 calendar commemorates him on August 18.
s721.intercession: St. Agapitus, pray for us, and for all young people. Amen.

s722.content:
Zephyrinus, a Roman, led the Church of Rome from 199 to 217. His chief helper was the deacon Callixtus, later pope, whom he put in charge of the Christian cemetery on the Appian Way that bears Callixtus’s name.

He defended faith in the divinity of Christ against the heresies of his day. The 1962 calendar commemorates him on August 26.
s722.intercession: St. Zephyrinus, pray for us. Keep us faithful to Christ, true God and true man. Amen.
